t: Abdulaziz recaptured Riyadh in 1902, took Al-Ahsa from the Ottomans in 1913 with the Ikhwan, conquered the Kingdom of Hejaz in 1924–25 and, after crushing the Ikhwan at the Battle of Sabilla in 1929, united Hejaz and Nejd as Saudi Arabia on 23 September 1932.

Oil found in Al-Ahsa in 1938 and developed by Aramco from 1941 made the kingdom the world's largest oil producer by 1976; the 1973 embargo quadrupled oil prices, and the state bought out Aramco's American owners in 1980.

The Al Saud rule as absolute monarchs under the Basic Law of 1992, with uncodified Sharia and the ulema, led by the Al ash-Sheikh, sharing power in a pact dating from 1744; no political parties or national elections are permitted.
dyk: Saudi Arabia's slave population was estimated at 300,000 as recently as the early 1960s; slavery was officially abolished only in 1962.
ev: On 23 September Prince Faisal declares on Ibn Saud's behalf the unification of the kingdoms of Hejaz and Nejd as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, now the Saudi National Day.
Vast oil reserves are discovered in Al-Ahsa on the Persian Gulf; full-scale development begins in 1941 under the American-controlled Aramco.
Saudi Arabia leads an oil embargo against the Western countries that supported Israel in the Yom Kippur War, and oil prices quadruple.

The Iranian Revolution and the seizure of the Grand Mosque in Mecca by Islamist militants, retaken after ten days, push the royal family towards stricter religious observance and a greater role for the ulema.
After Iraq invades Kuwait, King Fahd asks the United States to intervene and allows American and coalition troops to be stationed in the kingdom; Saudi forces join the Gulf War of 1991.
King Fahd introduces the Basic Law in March; the Consultative Council of sixty appointed members is inaugurated in December 1993.
Saudi Arabia mobilises 150,000 troops and 100 fighter jets to intervene in the civil war in Yemen; women vote and stand in municipal elections for the first time.
Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman takes power; as many as 500 princes, ministers and businessmen are arrested in an anti-corruption campaign in November.

f.founder: Abdulaziz, known as Ibn Saud, who recaptured Riyadh in 1902 and had the unification of Hejaz and Nejd declared on 23 September 1932
f.predecessor: The Sultanate of Nejd and the Kingdom of Hejaz, ruled as a dual kingdom from 1926; before them the Emirate of Diriyah (1727–1818) and the Emirate of Nejd (1824–1891), the First and Second Saudi States, and Ottoman suzerainty over the Hejaz
